correctness.rationale: Starting from the displayed modal polynomial, the positive endpoint root radius and negative endpoint radius reduce to the two closed branches in RESULT.md. On \(0<\beta\le1\), the average-mode factor decreases while both nonzero endpoint branches increase, so the minimizer is the first crossing. Solving the positive crossing gives \(1-\sqrt p\); solving the negative crossing gives the stated radical. Direct root calculations and independent one-dimensional minimization on representative positive-only, negative-only, and mixed endpoint pairs agree with the formula.

value.rationale: The sign of the extreme consensus eigenvalue is discarded by the standard essential-radius summary but materially changes the exact fixed-graph rate. The closed negative branch quantifies a real tuning gain on graphs with negative dominant spectrum and gives a natural graph-specific refinement of certified sign-blind tuning.
residual_risks: If full-source inspection later establishes that the same signed formula is already a direct corollary, value/originality should be revisited together.

final_claim: For homogeneous scalar quadratic distributed gradient tracking on a fixed connected symmetric doubly stochastic graph, if \(p=\max\{\lambda_2,0\}\) and \(n=\max\{-\lambda_N,0\}\), then the exact optimal normalized common stepsize is \(\beta_*=1-r_*\) with \(r_*=\max\{\sqrt p,(\sqrt{n(4+5n)}-n)/2\}\), and the attained spectral factor is \(r_*\).
limitations: Uniform scalar curvatures and one constant common stepsize only; no heterogeneous curvatures, directed/time-varying networks, or vector Hessians.
